# Clinical Assessment

This folder groups the clinical scoring systems and assessment tools used to evaluate patient risk, comorbidity, and physiological status in Danish acute surgery. The pages detail how models like the ASA classification, Charlson Score, APACHE, P-POSSUM, and the Surgical Apgar Score are applied—or rejected for being too cumbersome—within the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) to track quality indicators, predict mortality, and identify high-risk patients requiring extended postoperative observation.

## Pages

- [[apache|APACHE]] — An intensive care scoring system evaluated for preoperative mortality prediction in acute gastrointestinal surgery, but deemed too complex for routine use in national quality indicators.
- [[asa-score|ASA]] — The American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification, used to identify high-risk patients (score ≥ 3) and track regional variations in pre-operative health status.
- [[charlson-score-ge-3|Charlson Score ≥ 3]] — A comorbidity cohort definition used to track 30-day postoperative mortality among acute surgery patients with high registered comorbidity.
- [[p-possum|P-POSSUM]] — A postoperative risk scoring system that, like APACHE, was assessed by the AKDB steering committee as too comprehensive and burdensome for everyday clinical quality reporting.
- [[surgical-apgar-score|Surgical Apgar Score]] — An intraoperative scoring system criticized by the AKDB for failing to identify high-risk patients who do not exhibit physiological stress during surgery.
